result: Conclusion: DFTB3 is not universally bad, but its proton-transfer errors are chemical-group dependent and the Nyl12 zwitterion collapse requires a targeted benchmark. The 2025 Arantes/Rezac JCTC benchmark reports overall isolated-PT MUEs of 15.2 kJ/mol for DFTB3 and 13.5 kJ/mol for GFN2-xTB, but for the -NH3 subset DFTB3 is 14.4 and GFN2-xTB 22.2 kJ/mol, so GFN2 is not automatically better for the relevant ammonium chemistry. Recommended benchmark: actual N-terminal threonine methylamide neutral/zwitterion plus methanol/methylamine functional-group pair; compare DFTB3/3OB, GFN2-xTB, and omegaB97X-D with a diffuse triple-zeta basis on identical geometries and constrained proton-transfer curves at several O...N separations. Evaluate state ordering, reaction energy/proton affinity, barrier/location, and geometry; gas-phase PA alone is insufficient. No jobs launched.
